data.narrative:
Axiom Space is a Series G space infrastructure company founded by Michael T. Suffredini and Kam Ghaffarian, having raised $350M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of 13 comparable companies across Space & Aerospace (5 public: RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL; 8 private including SpaceX and Rocket Lab), though narrow peer trading multiples prove inaccessible for direct application.

Stage-progression methodology is the primary applicable valuation anchor. Using $175M as a proxy for total capital deployed, a typical 1.25x step-up multiplier for Series G progression yields an implied valuation of $219M. Peer-median triangulation is not viable; while 14 same-sector companies exist, insufficient clustering at identical or adjacent stages precludes robust median calibration. Public-comp P/S anchoring cannot be applied given absence of disclosed target revenue, a standard limitation for private-company analysis. Public Space & Aerospace multiples median 24.4x P/S across the five listed peers, providing directional context only.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $186M (low) to $252M (median $219M), centered on the stage-progression output. Key uncertainties include the absence of revenue visibility, limiting refinement via multiples-based methods, and the sparsity of precise peer comparables at Axiom's advancement stage. The range reflects early-stage methodological constraints rather than fundamental business uncertainty.
